disposition: met: target L2, level_met L2, measured 2026-10-01 against libclang 18.1.1's CompilationDatabase (tier A, calibration/oracles/clang-compdb) on CMake-generated databases (CMake 4.4.3, Unix Makefiles, arm64 macOS) of fmtlib/fmt 12.2.0 (51 entries) and libuv/libuv v1.53.0 (477 entries), written by calibration/oracles/clang-compdb/gen_compdb.sh into the checkout ROOT: no pinned subject commits a compile_commands.json, the databases are generated here, not the subjects', and ingest reads a root database only (build/ is excluded by .fathomignore's CT-8 default, so a database left in a build tree is never indexed; fusion.includeRoots reads compile_commands.json and build/compile_commands.json). Their file and directory fields are scratch-machine absolute paths. L1 excellent: sym_recall and sym_precision 1 over 528 units, range 1 (a CompileUnit per entry, named by its file as written, from the entry's opening brace to its closing one). L2 excellent: ref_recall and ref_precision 1 over 2,186 pairs (each unit's include directories, macros and -o output, written flag and argument together). The dialect reads the flags as fusion.includeRoots does (whitespace-split command, -I joined or separate, -iquote, -isystem and -idirafter separate only); clang's driver also reads those three joined to their directory and the oracle does, but neither subject writes one (O376, for item cinc). The output is the -o argument, else the entry's output field: CMake writes output relative to the top build directory and -o relative to the entry's directory, 48 of fmt's 51 entries differ, and the oracle reads the compiler's own flag. Throughput 65.6 MB per CPU-second (the doc engine, no grammar). L3 is not attempted (target L2). Dispatched: register.go claims compile_commands.json by basename ahead of the generic JSON extractor (TestIngest_CompileCommandsDialectIsDispatched).
